title: EU places ChatGPT under its strictest Digital Services Act tier
friendlyTitle: The EU gives ChatGPT stricter online-service rules
summary: The European Commission has designated ChatGPT a Very Large Online Search Engine after it reported at least 45 million average monthly EU users. OpenAI has four months to meet additional obligations covering systemic risk assessment, minors, wellbeing, illegal content, rights, elections and public security.
friendlySummary: The EU now treats ChatGPT as a very large online search service. OpenAI must follow stronger rules and explain how it manages major risks.
whyItMatters: ChatGPT is now being regulated partly as a search and information-discovery service, not only as an AI model. The designation could influence transparency, safety controls and product design for EU users and set expectations for other widely used assistants.
friendlyWhyItMatters: People in Europe may see stronger safety and transparency controls. Other large AI assistants may face similar rules as they grow.
